body.statement: Using \(\mathsf{Refine}\), can one construct a concrete serialized parser, generator, and executable exact-rational checker that refines \(\operatorname{Gen}\) and \(\operatorname{Verify}\) and prove, for every well-formed \(I\in\mathfrak I_{q,k}^{\ge3}\), the soundness, generator completeness, rational endpoint realization, and \(2^{O(q^2(k+1)^2)}\operatorname{poly}(B)\) bit bound asserted in \(\text{thm:verifier-refinement}\), while replaying \(\mathsf F_\star\) and rejecting a deleted necessary vertex, a corrupted separator entry, a singular-support misclassification, and a source-kernel mismatch?
body.justification: This is the load-bearing open content: the abstract finite algorithm must survive serialization, parser, arithmetic, and decoder refinement without weakening the causal guarantee.
body.gap: Li, Passmore, and Paulson establish the producer--checker architecture for univariate algebra, while causaloptim-lean covers linear causal certificates; neither supplies this multiblock support-and-separator refinement.
body.consumer: A portable certificate artifact can be independently replayed by causal-bound software and by a later proof-assistant implementation.
